title: Can't filter on property because indexFilterable is not enabled (but it is)
body:
Hi, I'm trying to make a filtered query on my `Article`, specifically on the `articleId` property.

Here is the result of `client.schema.get("Article")` (indexFilterable seems enabled on `articleId`):
```
{'class': 'Article',
 'description': 'Articles des différentes codes de la loi.',
 'invertedIndexConfig': {'bm25': {'b': 0.75, 'k1': 1.2},
  'cleanupIntervalSeconds': 60,
 'moduleConfig': {'text2vec-transformers': {'poolingStrategy': 'masked_mean',
   'vectorizeClassName': True}},
 'properties': [
  {'dataType': ['text'],
   'description': "Id unique Legifrance de l'article.",
   'indexFilterable': True,
   'indexSearchable': False,
   'moduleConfig': {'text2vec-transformers': {'skip': False,
     'vectorizePropertyName': False}},
   'name': 'articleId',
   'tokenization': 'word'},
  {'dataType': ['text'],
   'description': "Le titre de l'article.",
   'indexFilterable': True,
   'indexSearchable': True,
   'moduleConfig': {'text2vec-transformers': {'skip': False,
     'vectorizePropertyName': False}},
   'name': 'titre',
   'tokenization': 'word'},
  {'dataType': ['text'],
   'description': "Le texte de l'article.",

   'indexSearchable': True,
   'moduleConfig': {'text2vec-transformers': {'skip': False,
     'vectorizePropertyName': False}},
   'name': 'texte',
   'tokenization': 'word'},
  {'dataType': ['text'],
   'description': "Source juridique (code, loi ou ordonnance) contenant l'article.",
   'indexFilterable': True,
   'indexSearchable': True,
   'moduleConfig': {'text2vec-transformers': {'skip': False,
     'vectorizePropertyName': False}},
   'name': 'source',
   'tokenization': 'field'},
  {'dataType': ['text'],
   'description': "Chemin daccès à l'article (séparés par '>>')",
   'indexFilterable': True,
   'indexSearchable': True,
   'moduleConfig': {'text2vec-transformers': {'skip': False,
     'vectorizePropertyName': False}},
   'name': 'pathTitle',
   'tokenization': 'word'}],
 'replicationConfig': {'factor': 1},
 'shardingConfig': {'virtualPerPhysical': 128,
  'desiredCount': 1,
  'actualCount': 1,
  'desiredVirtualCount': 128,
  'actualVirtualCount': 128,
  'key': '_id',
  'strategy': 'hash',
  'function': 'murmur3'},
 'vectorIndexConfig': {'skip': False,
  'cleanupIntervalSeconds': 300,
  'maxConnections': 64,
  'efConstruction': 128,
  'ef': 2500,
  'dynamicEfMin': 100,
  'dynamicEfMax': 500,
  'dynamicEfFactor': 8,
  'vectorCacheMaxObjects': 50000000,
  'flatSearchCutoff': 40000,
  'distance': 'cosine',
  'pq': {'enabled': False,
   'bitCompression': False,
   'segments': 0,
   'centroids': 256,
   'encoder': {'type': 'kmeans', 'distribution': 'log-normal'}}},
 'vectorIndexType': 'hnsw',
 'vectorizer': 'text2vec-transformers'}
```

This is my query function :
```
async def get_article_from_id(source_id: str):
    query = '''
        query {
            Get {
                Article(
                    limit: 1,
                    where: {
                        path: ["articleId"],
                        operator: Equal,
                        valueString: "[[ID]]"
                    }) {
                    articleId
                    titre
                    pathTitle
                    texte
                    source
                }
            }
        }
    '''.replace("[[ID]]", source_id)

    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
        async with session.post(url, headers=headers, data=json.dumps({'query': query})) as response:
            return await response.json()
```


And here is the error I get :
```
{'data': {'Get': {'Article': None}}, 'errors': [{'locations': [{'column': 17, 'line': 4}], 'message': "Filtering by property 'articleId' requires inverted index. Is `indexFilterable` option of property 'articleId' enabled? Set it to `true` or leave empty", 'path': ['Get', 'Article']}]}
```

Does the error happen because `indexSearchable` is set to false ? In this case the error message is wrong – I prefer waiting your input before re-importing my whole DB over again.

Thanks a lot !! Weaviate is fantastic !

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hey @reporter. Thank you for reporting your issue.

Your configuration looks fine. `indexFilterable` enabled for `articleId` should be sufficient for query you are trying to execute.
What is weaviate version that you are currently using?
Is it the same version, data was imported to or did you upgrade on the way?
Do you have any problems with filtering by other text properties (I see only `articleId` has `indexSearchable` set to false)?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> Hey @reporter. Thank you for reporting your issue.
> 
> Your configuration looks fine. `indexFilterable` enabled for `articleId` should be sufficient for query you are trying to execute. What is weaviate version that you are currently using? Is it the same version, data was imported to or did you upgrade on the way? Do you have any problems with filtering by other text properties (I see only `articleId` has `indexSearchable` set to false)?

I’m on semitechnologies/weaviate:1.19.5 
It is possible I upgraded the weaviate instance after uploading the data! 

Anyway I deleted the whole class, recreated it (exactly like before) and now my queries work just fine.

Probably a version thing. Thanks !

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hey @reporter.
Do you remember if you started with 1.18.x or 1.19.x?
Before 1.19 there was only one setting `IndexInverted` which was then split to `IndexSearchable` and `IndexFilterable`. Maybe your issue is related to migration between those minor versions and setting adjustments done by weaviate in the background.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: @participant1 , I don't remember too well, it might be after 1.19 because I still have the code I used to create the class and I set up both `IndexInverted` and `IndexSearchable` for my Article class.

comments.body:
Actually nothing, it's a tough one to debug...
> Anyway I deleted the whole class, recreated it (exactly like before) and now my queries work just fine.
I just did that, without editing my class creation function nor the data.

My Weaviate use case concerns static data that needs to be updated once a while — for which I just delete the class and rebuild it with the new data, but the class never changes.

The weird part is I also have another class which I don't touch at all because the data is final, and no issue there.

Anyway for now it works because I rebuilt the class and re-uploaded the data, I'll try to get more details if it occurs again.

@participant1

Probably something caused by an update / migration as you mentionned...
